text:
{
  "background_info": "Student Name: Vikram Joshi
School: National Institute for Mentally Handicapped, Secunderabad
Grade / Class: Grade 8
Date of IEP Meeting: 19 October 2026
Disability Classification: Intellectual Disability (mild) under RPwD Act 2016
Dominant Language: Telugu and Hindi (spoken), English (functional)
Date Services Begin: 2 November 2026
Parent/Guardian Contact: Mr. Suresh Joshi and Mrs. Sunita Joshi (+91-9876543210)
Medical Alerts: None reported; physical health and motor vitality are good.",

  "academic_performance": "Present Level: Educational Achievement - Vikram Joshi is currently functioning below grade level in academic literature and advanced mathematics. He demonstrates functional literacy skills suitable for reading simple safety signs and single-step written cues, but requires adapted texts for multi-step instructions.
Present Level: Cognitive Ability - Vikram demonstrates strengths in concrete, hands-on visual-spatial reasoning and practical task execution, while experiencing difficulty with abstract reasoning, symbolic mathematics, and complex cognitive processing.
Present Level: Language Ability - Vikram exhibits clear verbal communication with strong social interaction skills among peers and teachers. He comprehends simple spoken directions effectively but requires visual prompts for multi-step linguistic commands.
Present Level: Learning Style - Vikram is a kinesthetic and visual learner who benefits significantly from step-by-step task analysis, visual schedule boards, direct demonstration, and structured physical practice.
Present Level: Rate of Progress - Vikram shows steady, stable progress when instruction is delivered using adapted visual aids, chunked task structures, and positive reinforcement in practical workshop settings.",

  "social_development": "Present Level: Social Relationships - Vikram demonstrates strong interpersonal and social communication skills, forming positive relationships with peers, job coaches, and teachers. He interacts respectfully and actively seeks peer engagement during team-based practical tasks.
Present Level: Self-Concept and Adjustment - Vikram exhibits high motivation, personal pride, and focus when engaging in hands-on activities. He responds very favorably to positive verbal reinforcement and systematic routines.
Present Level: Learning Behaviors - While highly cooperative during vocational sessions, Vikram experiences frustration when confronted with abstract written material or unstructured transitions. Structured visual supports maintain his task engagement and positive classroom behavior.",

  "physical_development": "Present Level: Motor and Sensory Development - Vikram displays age-appropriate gross and fine motor coordination, enabling proficient execution of manual assembly, material sorting, and workshop tool handling. Sensory processing is intact with no significant visual or auditory deficits.
Present Level: Health and Vitality - Vikram maintains good physical health and physical stamina throughout full-day vocational and academic schedules. His diagnosis of mild intellectual disability does not impede physical mobility or general health.",

  "management_needs": "Vikram requires a moderate level of environmental management and structural supports to succeed across educational and vocational settings. Environmental modifications include structured visual schedules, task-analyzed pictorial guideboards, and a predictable work environment free from auditory distractions during academic tasks.
Human and material resources required include access to a certified special educator, job coach support during practical vocational training, an occupational therapy consultant, and multi-disciplinary team coordination. Material supports involve adapted functional math workbooks, concrete manipulative sets, and simplified visual instruction cards.",

  "long_term_outcomes": "Post-Secondary Education and Training: Vikram aims to enroll in a structured post-secondary vocational training program focused on component assembly, packaging, or industrial material sorting. Transition services will provide guided vocational exposure, work-site visits, and practical skill refinement pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.32).
Employment Goals: Upon school completion, Vikram aspires to secure supported employment or competitive sheltered employment in a manufacturing or assembly setting, utilizing employment reservation provisions under Section 34 of the RPwD Act 2016.
Community Living Goals: Vikram will work toward independent community living, including safe travel, independent personal budgeting, and community navigation. Course requirements focus on functional academics, independent life skills, daily living skills, and practical vocational training.",

  "annual_goals": "Annual Goal: Vikram will independently assemble multi-component vocational items in a workshop environment.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Vikram will independently complete a 5-step assembly task with 100% accuracy across 4 out of 5 consecutive trials as measured by vocational workshop observational checklists and time logs.
2. By the end of Term 2, Vikram will independently complete an 8-step component assembly task with 90% accuracy across 4 out of 5 trials as measured by job coach observational checklists.
3. By the end of Term 3, Vikram will independently complete a 10-step component assembly task within a 15-minute timeframe with 90% accuracy across 5 consecutive trials as measured by workshop evaluation logs.
Evaluation Procedures: Observational checklists, timed task logs, job coach performance rubrics
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Vikram will demonstrate practical financial math skills for daily living transactions.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Vikram will correctly identify currency notes and coins up to 500 INR with 90% accuracy across 5 trials as measured by classroom math assessments.
2. By the end of Term 2, Vikram will accurately calculate correct change for practical transactions up to 500 INR with 85% accuracy across 4 out of 5 trials as measured by functional math practical assessment rubrics.
3. By the end of Term 3, Vikram will solve real-world store purchase scenarios involving multi-item transactions up to 500 INR with 90% accuracy as measured by practical transaction logs.
Evaluation Procedures: Practical math rubrics, simulated store assessment, teacher records
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly

Annual Goal: Vikram will complete a vocational internship while demonstrating workplace safety and punctuality.
Short-term Objectives:
1. By the end of Term 1, Vikram will adhere to workplace safety rules and visual schedule steps during simulated workshop sessions with 90% accuracy as measured by job coach observational checklists.
2. By the end of Term 2, Vikram will maintain attendance and punctuality rules during a 3-day internal campus work placement with 95% consistency as measured by timecard logs.
3. By the end of Term 3, Vikram will successfully complete a two-week external vocational internship demonstrating workplace safety and punctuality with an overall score of at least 80% as measured by employer evaluation sheets and job coach logs.
Evaluation Procedures: Employer evaluation sheets, job coach logs, daily attendance logs
Evaluation Schedule: Quarterly",

  "special_education_services": "A. Special Education Programs: Functional academic instruction adapted to cognitive level and life skills / daily living skills training provided by a certified special educator for 15 hours per week, beginning 2 November 2026 and continuing through 31 March 2027. Multi-disciplinary support schedule includes speech and language therapy (1 session per week) to support practical vocational communication, occupational therapy evaluation and monthly consultation to assess motor task ergonomic needs, and job coaching/vocational training for 10 hours per week under RPwD Act Section 31.

B. Extended School Year Services: No. Extended school year services are not required at this time as Vikram maintains skill retention over typical breaks.

C. Supplementary Aids and Modifications: Modified curriculum with simplified language and visual supports. Modified functional academic curriculum and flexible assessment tools as per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30). Task-analyzed step-by-step visual checklists for vocational and daily living activities. Transition planning including vocational guidance, post-secondary education, and community living under RPwD Act Section 31 and NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.32). Safe transition transport protocols and adequate transport facilities provided for all off-campus vocational site visits pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.32).

D. Assistive Technology Devices/Services: Provision of assistive technology including visual schedule boards, step-by-step pictorial task guides, and digital visual timers under NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30).

E. Program Modifications for School Personnel: Bi-weekly multi-disciplinary team coordination meetings between special educators, job coaches, occupational therapy consultants, and vocational instructors. Staff training on task analysis breakdown and positive reinforcement strategies.

F. Individual Testing Modifications: Extended time on assessments (minimum 25% extra time), simplified written instructions, visual prompt cards, flexible assessment tools as per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.30), and oral/practical demonstration options for functional academic and vocational testing.",

  "general_education_participation": "Vikram will participate with peers without disabilities during non-academic, vocational workshops, physical education, school assemblies, cultural events, and lunch periods for approximately 40% of the school week. He will receive specialized instruction in functional academics, life skills, and intensive vocational training in resource room settings for the remaining 60% of the time. No exemptions from general physical education are required. Second language exemptions or waivers are not sought as the curriculum focuses on functional language proficiency in primary regional and national languages.",

  "participating_agencies": "National Institute for Mentally Handicapped (NIMH), Secunderabad (lead institution);
District Disability Rehabilitation Centre (DDRC), Hyderabad;
Local vocational training institutes and community partner industrial workshops;
State Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.",

  "coordinated_activities": "1. Instruction: Functional academic instruction adapted to cognitive level focusing on practical reading and math.
2. Related Services: Speech and language therapy, occupational therapy evaluation and consultation, multi-disciplinary team support.
3. Employment/Post-secondary Education: Formal transition plan with clearly defined criteria, vocational guidance, supported job coaching, and industrial site visits pursuant to NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.32).
4. Community Experience: Community living training, travel training, safe transition transport protocols, and community shopping navigation.
5. Activities of Daily Living: Life skills training, independent money management, personal safety, and workplace hygiene.
6. Functional Vocational Assessment: Ongoing vocational task analysis, workshop performance checklists, and employer evaluations.",

  "graduation_info": "Certificate Sought: Special Vocational Certificate / Adapted Secondary School Completion Certificate issued in accordance with NIMH and State Board guidelines.
Expected Year of School Completion: Academic Year 2028-2029 (upon completion of secondary transition program).
Board Examination Provisions: Access to board accommodations under RPwD Act provisions, including modified functional evaluation tools, flexible assessment formats, and extended time on written tests. Second language requirements are adapted to functional literacy standards aligned with general curriculum decisions.",

  "recommendations_summary": "Disability Classification: Intellectual Disability (mild) under RPwD Act 2016.
Recommended Placement: Special education resource classroom combined with inclusive vocational workshops and community-based transition placements at NIMH, Secunderabad.
Extended School Year Services: Not recommended at present.
Transportation Needs: Safe transition transport protocols and structured bus transportation with escort support for vocational community trips as per NCTE/NCERT Guidelines (p.32).
Annual Review: Scheduled for 19 October 2027.",

  "progress_reporting": "Progress reporting to parents will occur at the same frequency as for non-disabled peers (quarterly). Progress will be reported using written quarterly goal progress reports, employer and job coach evaluation rubrics, and formal parent-teacher conferences scheduled at the end of each academic term. Parent meetings will review objective data from vocational task logs and functional academic assessments to monitor goal attainment."
}
